title: H999--SPS Water Sampling- Service Contract
description: SPS Water Sampling- Service Contract - RFI s Sample Location 8 is Steam.� It s listed as Utility Water not as Steam which would match Table 6.� Are we being requested to test Bacteria in this sample like Utility Water or N/A like Steam? Yes. We would need steam to be tested for bacteria on a quarterly basis. Onsite, when the water sampling is occurring, we have a team that will convert the steam into water and provide that sample to be tested for bacteria. Sample Locations 4-7 Medivators are typically listed as Utility Water but per Table 2 are held to Critical Water standard values as High-level Disinfection final rinse .� Are these to be tested monthly as Critical water or Quarterly as Utility Water? The Medivators would need to be tested monthly as critical water. The medivators run off of utility water from the City of Manchester and are not on the Osmosis system. Sample Location 12 is Re-looped Filter Osmosis ; VERDA interprets this as the Loop Return as described in Table 5 of ST108 which recommends Monthly testing of Bacteria and Endotoxin.� Is this location only to be tested upon failure of Table 6 results or as described in Table 5? The Re-looped filter Osmosis is sampling point off the Osmosis system. We determined that this location does not need to be sampled on a regular monthly or quarterly basis. We wanted to have this sampling point available incase of failures at other sample locations to test to get an comparable reading. We would estimate around 5 times per year we would need a water sample. Re-sampling is requested upon any failures within 48 hours of request.� Will this be at a set price in an added CLIN or issued as separate order? We would like the price of re-sampling to be a set price in an added CLIN. The Service contract would include routine sampling of the sampling points (monthly/quarterly) and re-sampling. The Statement of Work references Tables 5 and 6, which include references to Annex H and Annex I. Please confirm whether Annex H and Annex I refer to the corresponding annexes within ANSI/AAMI ST108:2023, or if there are separate VA-provided annexes that should be used for this requirement. Annex H and Annex I refers to the corresponding annexes within the ANSI/AAMI ST108:2023 standards. Tables 5 and 6 are references from these standards and VA Policy. The solicitation states that applicable labor rates must be provided so they can be compared to the applicable wage determination for Service Contract Labor Standards compliance. Please confirm the applicable wage determination number and revision for this requirement. Wage determination is with the Contracting Officer expertise. There is not a special labor rate needed for this request/requirement. Cost would be labor to perform the work in sampling/gathering/analysis the sample. Other costs would be any material used and etc direct costs. The price schedule only provides monthly line items. Are separate labor categories/rates required to be submitted with the quote, or is the completed line-item table sufficient? A completed line item table would be sufficient. Pricing can be based on a monthly or individual sampling basis. For the resample, we estimate to need around 6 for the sample locations (1, 2, & 3), 10 for sample locations (4, 5, 6, & 7), 4 for sample locations (8, 9, 10, 11). For sample location 12 we would 5 samples. This would be per fiscal year.

title: Udbud af drift og service af ladebokse i Udviklingsselskabet By & Havn I/S’ parkeringsanlæg
description: Nærværende udbud vedrører en kontrakt om overtagelse, drift, service, support, reparation, vedligeholdelse og – efter behov – udskiftning af ladebokse i Udviklingsselskabet By & Havn I/S’ (”By & Havn”) parkeringsanlæg (”Kontrakten”). Kontrakten omfatter ikke indkøb, projektering, etablering eller installation af nye ladepunkter/ladebokse, bortset fra udskiftning af defekte eller udtjente ladebokse og tilslutning/integration af sådanne erstatningsladebokse som led i driften. For en nærmere præcisering af opgaven henvises til Kontrakten med bilag, herunder kravspecifikationen (bilag 1). Leverandøren skal fra den 1. december 2026 begynde udrulningen af sin operatørplatform, herunder gennemføre de nødvendige forberedelser til, at By & Havns eksisterende ladebokse kan overgå i sin helhed til leverandørens platform og driftsmiljø pr. 1. januar 2027. Perioden fra den 1. december 2026 til og med den 31. december 2026 er en overgangs- og implementeringsperiode, hvor leverandøren ikke skal drifte, servicere, vedligeholde eller reparere selve ladeboksene, idet disse ydelser fortsat håndteres af By & Havns eksisterende leverandør, Spirii, til og med den 31. december 2026. Leverandøren overtager den fulde drifts-, service-, support-, vedligeholdelses- og reparationsforpligtelse for By & Havns eksisterende ladebokse fra den 1. januar 2027. By & Havn kan derudover i kontraktperioden anmode leverandøren om at overtage driften af nye ladebokse, som By & Havn får etableret af tredjemand i henhold til vilkårene i Kontrakten og bilagene hertil. Leverandøren er ansvarlig for driften fra det tidspunkt, hvor ladeboksene skriftligt er overtaget til drift under Kontrakten. Kontrakten træder i kraft ved underskrift og løber frem til og med den 31. december 2029, medmindre Kontrakten forlænges. By & Havn kan forlænge Kontrakten to (2) gange i op til 24 måneder ad gangen på uændrede vilkår. Kontrakten har en anslået værdi for hele perioden, inkl. optioner, på samlet DKK 20 mio. ekskl. moms. Den anslåede kontraktværdi er opgjort som den samlede forventede betaling til leverandøren i kontraktperioden på samlet 7 år, ekskl. moms, men inkl. de faste månedlige betalinger for drift og service af ladestanderne, udskiftning af defekte ladebokse, overtagelse af drift af eksisterende ladeinfrastruktur samt omsætningssplit pr. solgt kWh, beregnet på baggrund af By & Havns bedste skøn over det forventede strømforbrug samt øvrige betalinger til leverandøren.

title: Sweden – Health services – DVD/261012 - Monitoring of excess mortality across Europe for timely assessment of the impact of communicable diseases and public health threats
description: The purpose of this procurement is to develop and operate a comprehensive system for timely monitoring of all cause mortality in Europe as an indicator of the population level impact of communicable diseases and other major public health threats. Excess all-cause mortality is a basic indicator for the assessment of the impact of influenza epidemics in the general population and an understanding of its epidemiology is key for effective public health planning and action. The most widely accepted and utilised methodology for estimating influenza mortality is to model this from time-series data of all-cause mortality. Vital statistics are accessible for all European countries, but might not be available in a timely fashion. The variation of mortality rates within a population over time can be ascribed to different factors as extreme weather conditions as well as waves of respiratory diseases as seen during the seasonal influenza epidemic. The monitoring of all-cause mortality provides valuable information on the general population and specific age-groups not targeted by disease-specific surveillance systems. Timely monitoring of excess mortality may also provide early warning signals for community-wide acute health effects. The objective of this tender is to establish and maintain a network of European Union, European Economic Area and Stabilisation and Association Agreement (EU/EEA/SAA) countries national institutes / study sites engaged in mortality monitoring and ensure monitoring of excess all-cause mortality in the EU as a mean to assess the impact of the respiratory viruses, mainly: seasonal and pandemic influenza, pandemic-prone coronaviruses such as SARS-CoV-2, and respiratory syncytial virus. The network and the methodology will build on the work done by the ‘Excess mortality monitoring in Europe to assess impact of communicable diseases’ project during 2022-2026. The analyses and outputs will be done in collaboration with activities covered by other similar supranational/global initiatives, with the capacity to serve and support EU/EEA/SAA countries. In order to ensure sustainability of project outcomes, the project will develop data collection, analysis and outputs in close collaboration with ECDC to enable handover of activities to ECDC, should this be requested. The overall objectives of this call for tender are: 1. To develop and maintain a network of EU Member State national authorities or study sites engaged or planning to engage in excess mortality monitoring. 2. To develop and maintain continuous and timely data collection processes, analytical methods and timely outputs for estimating expected mortality and identifying excess all-cause mortality monitoring across age groups and geographic areas. 3. To assess and analyse the impact of influenza, SARS-CoV-2, RSV and other epidemic or pandemic respiratory virus circulation on all-cause excess mortality. 4. To build and strengthen capacity in EU Member States for implementing harmonised mortality monitoring methodologies for all-cause excess mortality. 5. To disseminate analytical outputs in scientific, professional and public fora, and to support ECDC in integrating excess mortality findings into respiratory virus surveillance outputs. 6. To ensure uninterrupted excess all-cause mortality monitoring during a pandemic, extreme environmental events or an unexpected major public health event. 7. To ensure close collaboration with ECDC to support methodological alignment, data integration, and preparedness for a potential future transfer of activities.

buyer: European Union Agency For Law Enforcement Training
title: Hungary – Subscription services – Scientific e-journals and e-books: subscription, access and related services
description: The need for a dedicated tender arises from the increasingly central role of scientific knowledge in law enforcement training, research, and practice. Policing and security are no longer shaped only by professional experience or internal doctrine, but also by empirical research, data analysis, and interdisciplinary evidence. Access to peer-reviewed academic publications is therefore essential to ensure that training content, analytical work, and operational methodologies are informed by reliable, current, and validated knowledge. Without a formal procurement mechanism, access to such resources would remain fragmented, uneven, and dependent on ad hoc arrangements, creating a risk that parts of the community rely on incomplete or outdated information. A dedicated tender is therefore necessary to secure stable, lawful, and comprehensive access to high-quality scientific e-journals and e-books across the CEPOL community. The tender is also needed to ensure equal and organised access for all relevant users, including trainers, analysts, researchers, and operational staff. In the absence of a structured contractual framework, access to scientific literature is likely to vary between institutions and individuals, undermining consistency in training delivery, limiting the dissemination of best practices, and reducing the overall coherence of professional development across jurisdictions. Centralised procurement will support a common knowledge base, strengthen harmonisation in law enforcement education, and reinforce CEPOL’s role as a hub for knowledge exchange and evidence-based learning. Finally, the tender is necessary to address the technical and economic specificities of accessing licensed academic content in a controlled, sustainable, and cost-effective manner. Scientific publishers generally rely on specific licensing, authentication, and access-management systems, which must be compatible with CEPOL’s existing digital environment. Without a procurement procedure tailored to these requirements, there is a significant risk of selecting solutions that are technically unsuitable, financially inefficient, or dependent on costly bespoke development. By defining clear technical requirements and prioritising solutions that can be implemented within the existing environment, the tender ensures operational feasibility, protects institutional resources, and guarantees continuity and reliability of access to essential scientific knowledge.

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Umbau der Staustufe Königs Wusterhausen / Nottekanal mit Schleuse
description: Der Nottekanal im Vorhabensgebiet ist ein schiffbares Gewässer und wird der I. Ordnung zugeordnet. Der Nottekanal quert bei Fluss-km 1+730 den Straßendamm der Schlossstraße. Unmittelbar oberhalb der Straßenquerung befindet sich die Schleuse Königs Wusterhausen und die Ausleitung des Nottekanals hin zum ehemaligen Mühlenwehr. Die Einmündung des Mühlenkanals befindet sich bei km 1+450 auf der linken Gewässerseite. Die vorhandene komplexe Stauanlage am Standort besteht aus dem Mühlenwehr, das sich in der Ausleitungsstrecke befindet, dem Staudamm (Straßendamm/ Schleuseninsel), einem Hochwasserschutzwehr (Doppelrohrdurchlass zwischen Schleuseninsel und Mühlenkomplex; Hochwasserschutzablass) und der Verkehrsanlage (Schleuse mit oberem und unterem Vorhafen). Baulastträger der Schleusenanlage einschließlich der Vorhafenanlagen ist das Land Brandenburg, vertreten durch das Landesamt für Umwelt (LfU). Letzterem obliegen auch die Aufgaben des gesetzlichen Hochwasserschutzes und der Gewässerunterhaltung des Nottekanals als Wasserstraße und Gewässer I. Ordnung. Im Jahr 2019 erfolgte durch die Bauprüfstelle des Landesamtes für Umwelt eine aktualisierte einfache Prüfung des Bauzustandes. Die Anlage wurde in der Gesamteinschätzung mit der Bauzustandsnote 3 bewertet. Die Anlage befindet sich in einem befriedigenden Zustand. Standsicherheit und Gebrauchstauglichkeit sind nur eingeschränkt gegeben. Die Anlagentechnik ist aufgrund veralteter Technik nur eingeschränkt funktionsfähig und entspricht nicht den aktuell anerkannten Regeln der Technik. Im Jahr 2022 erfolgte durch das LfU eine erneute Prüfung des Bauzustandes. In dieser wurde die Anlage aufgrund der erheblichen Schäden und der fehlenden Gebrauchstauglichkeit in der Gesamteinschätzung mit der Zustandsnote 5 bewertet. In dieser aktualisierten Stellungnahme wurde ein Ersatzneubau der Schleuse empfohlen. Die Schleuse ist seit April 2022 außer Betrieb. Aus der zuvor beschriebenen/ dargestellten Situation leiten sich erforderliche Maßnahmen zum Umbau der Schleuse Königs Wusterhausen mit Ergänzung einer Hochwasserentlastung (Entkopplung Hochwasserentlastung und Schleuse) ab. Das Hochwasserentlastungsbauwerk soll unter Berücksichtigung der Hydrologischen Fachauskunft mit der erforderlichen Anzahl von Verschlüssen (n-1 Bedingungen) und einer für den Standort optimalen Verschlussart hergestellt werden. title: Germany – Construction work – Sanierung historisches Rathaus - Wärme-/Kälteerzeugung
description: Das Leistungsverzeichnis umfasst das Gewerk der Wärme-/Kältererzeugung. Das Rathaus Stolberg soll im Zweileiterprinzip sowohl beheizt als auch gekühlt werden. Hierfür ist der Einsatz einer Sole-Wasser-Wärmepumpe vorgesehen. Als Energiequelle dient eine Kombination aus Eisspeicher und Luftabsorber; optional werden Stutzen vorgesehen hier kann später zusätzlich eine Eislaufbahn integriert werden. Der Luftabsorber übernimmt im Sommer zudem die Rückkühlung im Kältebetrieb. Die Kühlenergie wird bevorzugt nachts, bei niedrigen Außentemperaturen, generiert. Durch die Größe des Eisspeichers ist eine tägliche Kälteproduktion nicht erforderlich und kann in Zeiten verlagert werden, an denen die Außentemperatur zur Rückkühlung moderat ist. Die Umschaltung zwischen Heiz- und Kühlbetrieb erfolgt über die vorgesehenen Umschaltventile in Abhängigkeit der Jahreszeit. Im Heizbetrieb wird dem flüssigen Wasser im Eisspeicher Energie entzogen bis es gefriert. Im Kühlbetrieb wird dem Eisspeicher direkt kaltes Wasser entnommen und über einen Wärmeübertrager zur Gebäudekühlung bereitgestellt. Das Wärme- bzw. Kälteerzeugungssystem wird an ein bauseits bestehendes Heiznetz angeschlossen. Das System besteht im Wesentlichen aus den Komponenten: - Eisspeicher - Luftabsorber - Wärmepumpe - Hydraulikmodul - Regelmodul - Hydraulische Verbindungssystem Im Kellergeschoss muss für das System ein Pufferspeicher eingebracht werden. Außerdem wird der Eisspeicher im gleichen Kellerraum aufgebaut. Aufgrund der Einbringmöglichkeiten wird der Speicher in Segmenten in den Keller transportiert und Vorort zusammengebaut. Im Erdgeschoss wird im Technikraum die Wärmepumpe und eine Hydraulik-Einheit untergebracht. Die Wärmepumpe soll das bereits bauseits bestehende Heiznetz versorgen. Die Hydraulik-Einheit ist die Schnittstelle zwischen der Wärmepumpe sowie den Energiequellen und ermöglicht die Nutzung bzw. Regeneration des Eisspeichers. Die Steuerung der Hydraulik-Einheit nimmt die Funktion des intelligenten Energiequellenmanagements beider Quellen ein. Darüber hinaus ermöglicht es die Regeneration des Energiespeichers bzw. des sich darin befindenden Quellenmediums (Wasser im Energiespeicher). Im Außenbereich wird der Luftabsorber nordwestlich neben dem Gebäude auf ein bauseitiges Fundament montiert. Der Luftabsorber überträgt die Umgebungswärme und wird für die Regeneration des Eisspeichers verwendet. Der Kellerraum zur Aufstellung des Eisspeichers und des Pufferspeichers ist ca. 7,9 m x 18,6 m groß, mit einer Deckenhöhe von ca. 2,39 m. Der Zuweg zu dem Kellerraum ist durch ein Treppenhaus (3,6 m x 5,4 m) mit Podesttreppe (Breite >1,4m) möglich. Die Türöffnungen im KG sind 1,00 m x 2,00 m. Im EG ist das Treppenhaus (6,6 m x 9,9 m) größer und reicht bis zur westlichen Eingangstür (Öffnungsmaß 1,16 m x 2,00 m). Der Technikraum hat die Maße ca. 3,5 m x 4,8 m und eine Deckenhöhe von ca. 3,1 m. Die Türöffnung des Technikraums hat die Maße 0,94 m x 2,00 m. Für die Aufstellung der Hydraulik-Einheit und der Wärmepumpe steht eine Fläche von ca. 2,6 m x 2,2 m zur Verfügung. Der Technikraum grenzt direkt an das westliche Treppenhaus

title: Germany – Environmental issues consultancy services – 10027690-Entwicklung und Implementierung strategischer Maßnahmen und Innovation zum Schutz des Tropenwaldes in Amazonien
description: Die größten zusammenhängenden Tropenwälder liegen in Amazonien, davon ca. 4,2 Mio. km2 in Brasilien. Sie speichern enorme Mengen Kohlenstoff und sind zentral für Klima und Biodiversität. Nahezu 20 % der ursprünglichen Waldbedeckung gingen durch Rinderweiden, Agrarflächen, Bergbau und Infrastruktur verloren. Der Aktionsplan zur Prävention und Kontrolle der Entwaldung in Amazonien (PPCDAm) steuert die sektorübergreifende Entwaldungsbekämpfung, sodass seit 2023 die großflächige Entwaldung um 50 % auf 5.796 km2 sank. Zunehmende Walddegradierung gefährdet die Fortschritte: 2024 verfünffachte sich die degradierte Fläche, vor allem durch Vegetationsbrände (Klimawandel, Brandstiftung, kleinflächige Abholzung). Der PPCDAm kombiniert unmittelbare Kontrolle mit raumordnerischen, bodenrechtlichen, ordnungspolitischen und ökonomischen Instrumenten. Er umfasst vier Achsen, zwölf strategische Ziele und 194 Aktionslinien, getragen von 13 Ministerien und Behörden. Die Steuerung erfolgt durch eine Interministerielle Kommission und eine Exekutivkommission im Umweltministerium MMA. Die Kapazitäten in Umweltbehörden und MMA sowie die Kooperation zwischen Ressorts und Bundesstaaten sowie Abläufe der Umweltkontrolle und des Schutzgebietsmanagements sind unzureichend. Effektive Instrumente für Feuermanagement und Wiederherstellung fehlen. Schwach gesicherte Land- und Nutzungsrechte indigener und traditioneller Gemeinschaften sowie strukturelle Benachteiligung von Frauen verschärfen die Lage; Kriminalität beeinträchtigt die Sicherheit und Vollzugsarbeit. Chancen: Hohe Priorität der Regierung für Waldschutz, NDC-Ziel Null-Entwaldung bis 2030 und Wiederherstellung von 12 Mio. ha. Politische Grundlagen: PPCDAm, nationale Politik für integriertes Feuermanagement (MIF) und Nationaler Plan zur Wiederherstellung der natürlichen Vegetation (PLANAVEG). Projektziel: Die Umsetzung der Politik zum Schutz des Tropenwaldes in Amazonien ist verbessert. Zielgruppen: Umweltinstitutionen auf föderaler, bundesstaatlicher und kommunaler Ebene sowie traditionelle Völker und Gemeinschaften. Mittler*innen: Fach- und Führungskräfte des MMA, föderale Umweltkontrollbehörde IBAMA, föderale Schutzgebietsbehörde ICMBio. Politischer Partner: MMA; Durchführungspartner: Sondersekretariat für Entwaldungskontrolle (SECD, Koordination PPCDAm). Output 1: Stärkung der strategischen Steuerung/Koordination der Entwaldungsbekämpfung; Analyse der Wirksamkeit von PPCDAm und Zusammenarbeit; bessere Kommunikation zu Nutzungsrechten traditioneller Gruppen; Stärkung von ICMBio-Management; systematische Genderintegration. Output 2: Stärkung von Überwachung und Kontrolle; Optimierung administrativer Sanktionsprozesse (Rechenschaft bei Umweltverstößen); Fortbildungen für IBAMA, ICMBio und Bundesstaaten/Munizipien; verbesserte Differenzierung legaler vs. illegaler Brände/Abholzung zur Erreichung von Null-Entwaldung. Output 3: Breite Verankerung des integrierten Feuermanagements (MIF) mit Genderbezug; Sensibilisierung, Ausbildungsstrategie, Richtlinien für Bundesstaaten/Gemeinden; Unterstützung der Regulierungsarbeit und Beschlussvorschläge; Einbindung traditioneller Gemeinschaften. Output 4: Stärkung von MMA für Wiederherstellung; Erfassung wiederhergestellter Flächen zur Steuerung von PLANAVEG; Schließen strategischer Lücken in Wertschöpfungsketten (Geschäftsmodelle, Professionalisierung von Saatgut/ Baumschulen); Einbindung Privatsektor, Mobilisierung privater Investitionen; Lenkung von Strafzahlungen in Wiederherstellungsinvestitionen (mit IBAMA).

title: CYROPHONE (cPhone)
description: NOTICE OF INTENT This notice is not a request for competitive quotes. NAVSUP FLCSD intends to award a sole-source contract. The NAVSUP Fleet Logistics Center San Diego (FLCSD) intends to solicit and award a firm-fixed-price (FFP) contract on a sole-source basis to Loggerhead Instruments (CAGE: 5KBN4, POC Email: dmann@loggerhead.com), 5342 Clark Road, Suite #187, Sarasota, FL 34233, using commercial acquisition procedures applicable to this requirement. The statutory authority for this noncompetitive action is FAR 12.102(a), Only one source is available, pursuant to 41 U.S.C. 1901. NAVSUP FLCSD intends to use commercial acquisition procedures applicable to this requirement. The Government has determined that Loggerhead Instruments is the only known responsible source capable of meeting the Government�s requirement within the required schedule and acceptable technical risk. The Government�s requirement is for the design, fabrication, integration, and delivery of a cryophone (�cPhone�) instrument to be deployed in the Arctic ice sheet in support of a new monitoring and detection system for Arctic research. The cPhone must meet the following functional performance criteria: reliable and accurate 4-channel recording sampling frequencies of at least 96 kHz bandwidth of 1 Hz to 48 kHz sensor sensitivity of 10 volts/g operation in air temperatures as low as -50 �F endurance of 12 months local storage of all raw data onboard statistical and Fourier analysis daily relay of reduced data and results via the Iridium satellite network flotation for deployment in the marginal ice zone (MIZ) The Government has determined that Loggerhead Instruments recently designed and built optical accelerometer drifters and a related 4-channel datalogger with the same general system architecture, electronics, firmware approach, telemetry concept, and deployment design as the required cPhone instrument. The Government further determined that the cPhone differs principally in the sensing element and represents an adaptation of a recently completed and validated system rather than a clean-sheet design. Award to another source would require substantial duplicative engineering effort and would introduce unacceptable schedule risk. The NAICS code for this procurement is 334519, Other Measuring and Controlling Device Manufacturing. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 6655. The required delivery date is 1 January 2027 to allow sufficient time for bench testing and validation before a planned February/March2027 Arctic field experiment in the Beaufort Sea. This notice is issued solely for market research and to determine whether other responsible sources can meet the Government�s minimum requirements. Interested parties may submit documentation demonstrating their ability to satisfy the Government�s requirement. Questions regarding this notice must be submitted by email to Allaine Benson at allaine.g.benson.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 3:00 PM PDT on 03 September 2026. Responses, if provided, will be posted publicly through SAM.gov. Capability Statement Requirements Interested parties shall submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to satisfy the Government�s minimum requirements. At a minimum, the capability statement shall address the vendor�s technical capability, relevant experience, and ability to provide a system with 4-channel high-rate recording, 1 Hz to 48 kHz bandwidth, 10 volts/g sensor performance, 12-month Arctic endurance, local raw-data storage, onboard statistical and Fourier analysis, daily Iridium telemetry, and flotation suitable for marginal ice zone deployment. Submission Instruction Length Constraint Submissions must not exceed 6 pages in 10-point Times New Roman font. This market research is solely to determine if technical capabilities exist in the marketplace. Requests for information or submissions with only questions are not affirmative responses. The results of this assessment will help the Government determine whether qualified sources exist and inform the decision on whether to continue with sole-source procurement or pursue competition. Point of Contact Please submit capability statements by email as a Word or PDF attachment to Allaine Benson at allaine.g.benson.civ@us.navy.mil by 3:00pm PDT, 07 September 2026. Please ensure all submissions are addressed to the listed contact to avoid any delays or missed deadlines.

title: NOTICE OF INTENT TO CONTRACT WITH A SINGLE SOURCE: Airport Express
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO CONTRACT WITH A SINGLE SOURCE: Airport Express . NOTICE OF INTENT TO CONTRACT WITH A SINGLE SOURCE: The Federal Aviation Administration Academy, intends to award a single source contract to Airport Express, Oklahoma City, OK for proposed FAA Academy transportation services to/from specific lodging properties and the Mike Monroney Aeronautical Center (MMAC) for students attending training at the Center. In accordance with the FAA Acquisition Management System, AMS 3.2.2.4, the purpose of this announcement is to inform industry of the basis of the FAA's decision to contract with a selected source when it is determined to be in the best interest of the FAA. This procurement is considered to be single-sourced to Airport Express based on the following: Transportation services under this requirement are integral to FAA Academy training execution, directly supporting the development of certified air traffic controllers and aviation personnel. The FAA Academy is currently operating under increased training throughput driven by national hiring initiatives to address air traffic controller staffing shortages. Any disruption in transportation services would: � Delay or cancel scheduled training events � Interrupt simulator and classroom progression � Impact student throughput and graduation timelines � Degrade FAA�s ability to meet national airspace staffing requirements Airport Express is the only vendor that has: � Consistently and clearly performed within the MMAC operational environment � Maintained a fully compliant fleet and cleared workforce � Successfully executed high-volume, schedule-driven transportation operations � Established existing routes, logistics coordination, and training integration o This vendor has a comprehensive understanding of FAA Academy training schedules, transportation routes, security access procedures, and coordination requirements necessary to support the movement of large volumes of students between facilities. This action represents a controlled, time-bound approach to: � Ensure continuity of mission-critical services � Allow the Government to refine requirements and acquisition strategy � Position the requirement for potential future competition under improved conditions The FAA is actively reassessing: � Service scope and capacity requirements � Cost drivers and efficiencies � Opportunities to expand vendor participation This announcement is for informational purposes only and not a Solicitation/Request for Proposal. This requirement will be awarded to Airport Express Oklahoma City, OK and is not available for full and open competition. All questions pertaining to this announcement should be addressed in writing to the Contract Specialist, Gilbert Park, gilbert.n.park@faa.gov, no later than Monday, September 7, 2026.

description: NOTICE OF INTENT This notice is not a request for competitive quotes. NAVSUP FLCSD intends to award a sole-source contract. The NAVSUP Fleet Logistics Center San Diego (FLCSD) intends to solicit and award a firm-fixed-price (FFP) contract on a sole-source basis to Loggerhead Instruments (CAGE: 5KBN4, POC Email: dmann@loggerhead.com), 5342 Clark Road, Suite #187, Sarasota, FL 34233, using commercial acquisition procedures applicable to this requirement. The statutory authority for this noncompetitive action is FAR 12.102(a), Only one source is available, pursuant to 41 U.S.C. 1901. NAVSUP FLCSD intends to use commercial acquisition procedures applicable to this requirement. The Government has determined that Loggerhead Instruments is the only known responsible source capable of meeting the Government�s requirement within the required schedule and acceptable technical risk. The Government�s requirement is for the design, fabrication, integration, and delivery of a cryophone (�cPhone�) instrument to be deployed in the Arctic ice sheet in support of a new monitoring and detection system for Arctic research. The cPhone must meet the following functional performance criteria: reliable and accurate 4-channel recording sampling frequencies of at least 96 kHz bandwidth of 1 Hz to 48 kHz sensor sensitivity of 10 volts/g operation in air temperatures as low as -50 �F endurance of 12 months local storage of all raw data onboard statistical and Fourier analysis daily relay of reduced data and results via the Iridium satellite network flotation for deployment in the marginal ice zone (MIZ) The Government has determined that Loggerhead Instruments recently designed and built optical accelerometer drifters and a related 4-channel datalogger with the same general system architecture, electronics, firmware approach, telemetry concept, and deployment design as the required cPhone instrument. The Government further determined that the cPhone differs principally in the sensing element and represents an adaptation of a recently completed and validated system rather than a clean-sheet design. Award to another source would require substantial duplicative engineering effort and would introduce unacceptable schedule risk. The NAICS code for this procurement is 334519, Other Measuring and Controlling Device Manufacturing. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 6655. The required delivery date is 1 January 2027 to allow sufficient time for bench testing and validation before a planned February/March2027 Arctic field experiment in the Beaufort Sea. This notice is issued solely for market research and to determine whether other responsible sources can meet the Government�s minimum requirements. Interested parties may submit documentation demonstrating their ability to satisfy the Government�s requirement. Capability Statement Requirements Interested parties shall submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to satisfy the Government�s minimum requirements. At a minimum, the capability statement shall address the vendor�s technical capability, relevant experience, and ability to provide a system with 4-channel high-rate recording, 1 Hz to 48 kHz bandwidth, 10 volts/g sensor performance, 12-month Arctic endurance, local raw-data storage, onboard statistical and Fourier analysis, daily Iridium telemetry, and flotation suitable for marginal ice zone deployment. Submission Instruction Length Constraint Submissions must not exceed 6 pages in 10-point Times New Roman font. This market research is solely to determine if technical capabilities exist in the marketplace. Requests for information or submissions with only questions are not affirmative responses. The results of this assessment will help the Government determine whether qualified sources exist and inform the decision on whether to continue with sole-source procurement or pursue competition. description: 1. General Information Document Type: Special Notice (Notice of Intent to Sole Source) Notice/Reference Number: 202607270001 Posted Date: 1 Sept 2026 Response Date: September 7, 2026, by 4:00 PM PDT NAICS Code: 333994 � Industrial Process Furnace and Oven Manufacturing Product Service Code (PSC): 4430 � Industrial Furnaces, Kilns, Lehrs, and Ovens Contracting Office: Air Force Test Center, Installation Contracting Division (AFTC/PZIOB), Edwards AFB, CA 93524 Subject: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Delta H Defender Series Dual Chamber Aerospace Heat Treating Furnace System 2. Description of Requirement The 412th Maintenance Squadron (412 MXS/MXMF) at Edwards AFB, CA, has a critical requirement for a dual-chamber, high-temperature, inert-atmosphere furnace system. This acquisition is prompted by the addition of new alloys requiring pre- and post-heat treatment after welding, as well as the implementation of new steel alloys in aircraft and engine components. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate a sole-source contract for this equipment under the authority of RFO 12.102(a) (restricting competition to a single source for simplified acquisitions). The designated equipment is: Manufacturer: Delta H Technologies, LLC. Model: DEF-DC-RH-241236/2000-RH-241636/2000-SR (Delta H Defender Series Dual Chamber Aerospace Heat Treating Furnace System) Authorized Federal Distributor: Phillips Corporation, Federal Division (identified by the OEM as the sole authorized distributor of this product to the United States Federal Government) 3. Comprehensive Technical Specifications To satisfy the requirements of RFO 12.202(a) and ensure transparency, the technical specifications and components of the equipment being procured are detailed below: A. Performance and Electrical Parameters Temperature Range: 500�F to 2,000�F Electrical Requirements: 480V, 3-Phase, 60 Hz, 100 Amps, 51 kW Overall Equipment Dimensions: 90� High x 66� Wide x 102� Long Total Approximate Weight: 5,500 lbs Inert Atmosphere: Gas-tight chambers with independent gas flow control and flow alarms. Structural Features: Oxidation-resistant lining, heavy-duty casters, and temperature-recording thermocouples. Quench System: Roll-away oil quench tank with a 16" high part capacity. B. Chamber Specifications The system consists of two independently operated chambers with the following dimensions and characteristics: Upper Chamber (Work Volume: 24" W x 12" H x 36" D): Certified Temperature Uniformity Survey (TUS) Work Volume. Radiant Heat Chamber rated to 2,000�F. Meets Class 3 standards (�15?F uniformity across the range of 1,200�F to 2,000�F). Gas-tight design with independent gas flow control and flow alarm. Lower Chamber (Work Volume: 24" W x 16" H x 36" D): Certified Temperature Uniformity Survey (TUS) Work Volume. Radiant Heat Chamber rated to 2,000�F. Meets Class 3 standards (�15?F uniformity across the range of 1,200�F to 2,000�F). Gas-tight design with independent gas flow control and flow alarm. C. Control, Instrumentation, and Monitoring Systems Primary Controller: Eurotherm programmable dual recorder/controller for independent program operations (supporting set-point or programmable profile modes). Process Recorder: Digital Paperless Process Recorder equipped with tamper-proof Batch Reporting and AMS2750 Process Monitoring Software. The recorder is configured to track thermocouple usage, TUS, System Accuracy Tests (SAT), and calibration intervals. Safety Controls: High-limit safety interlocks to ensure safe operation, facility safety, and product protection. Instrumentation Type: Type C Instrumentation, recording TUS High & Low locations, Air Control Temperature, and independent Quench Temperature. Test Ports: One dedicated, fixed SAT test port located adjacent to the control thermocouples. Nine designed-in TUS test ports built directly into the furnace structure for rapid TUS/SAT execution. D. Sensors, Probes, and Consumables (3-Year Support Package) Control/Monitoring Probes: All necessary Inconel-sheathed, non-expendable Type K thermocouple probes for both 2,000�F chambers, including five spare probes. Probes must feature individual serial numbers and large tags with NIST-traceable certificates to document installation/replacement dates and usage for compliance with TO 1-1A-9 and AMS2750H. SAT Thermocouples (Year 1): One-year supply of Type N thermocouples with NIST calibration certificates. Includes nine TUS probe thermocouples and a wire harness to connect to the Government-supplied super-systems TUS Recorder. 3-Year Operational Thermocouples (Type K): Includes annual replacement sets, spares, and a dedicated TUS probe set with wire harness. 3-Year SAT Thermocouples (Type N): Includes Type N thermocouples with connector cables conforming to AMS2750 requirements (12 thermocouples for quarterly replacement cycles plus two spares). E. Upgrades, Services, and Shipping 1 each � DEF-UPGRADE-DUAL: Upgrade Kit and Dual Chamber Services ensuring full compliance to SAE-AMS2750 and Boeing BAC5621 standards. 1 each � DEF-AQDTF: Automated Quench Delay Timer Function. 1 each � DEF-STARTUP: Four (4) days of on-site qualifying, calibration, and training services. 1 each � IUID_TA: Item Unique Identification (IUID) Tag Plate in compliance with MIL-STD-130x. 1 each � Freight Service: Inside delivery to Edwards AFB, CA. Warranty: Comprehensive two-year manufacturer warranty. Period of Performance / Delivery: 10�12 weeks After Receipt of Order (ARO). 4. Justification for Single Source The 412 MXS/MXMF currently operates Delta H Tool Master Furnaces and associated calibration equipment. This specific acquisition of the Delta H Defender Series Dual Chamber Furnace is justified by the following operational parameters: Interoperability & Training: The existing shop utilizes Eurotherm Nanodac controllers and current Delta H calibration accessories. Acquiring this system ensures seamless integration and eliminates the need for additional operator training or the acquisition of separate, proprietary testing and calibration hardware. Proprietary Systems: Market research indicates that alternative manufacturers utilize proprietary control systems that do not interface with the current Delta H system architecture or Eurotherm Nanodac controllers, making competitive options technically non-viable without costly infrastructure duplication. Exclusivity: Delta H Technologies, LLC. is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM). The OEM has formally established Phillips Corporation, Federal Division, as the sole and exclusive distributor of Delta H Furnaces and Ovens to all United States Government facilities. 5. Invitation for Capability Statements This notice of intent is NOT a request for competitive proposals or a solicitation for offers. However, in accordance with RFO requirements, the Government will consider capability statements from interested parties. Any alternative vendor or manufacturer who believes they can meet the exact technical, interoperability, and calibration requirements (without requiring the government to purchase new calibration accessories, duplicate software, or conduct additional technical training) is invited to submit a capability statement. Responses must include the following information: Company Profile: Company Name, CAGE Code, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), and Point of Contact (POC) information. Socioeconomic Status: Business size status under the applicable NAICS code (333994). Alternative Product Details (if applicable): Comprehensive technical data demonstrating how the proposed alternative product matches the exact physical dimensions, electrical requirements, operating temperatures, and calibration requirements of the Delta H system, including proof of seamless interoperability with current Eurotherm Nanodac controllers and existing Delta H calibration accessories.
